newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica president gets threat, grenades found.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica president gets threat, grenades found.

text.p: Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres dismissed as a "bad joke" on Thursday a telephone threat and the discovery of two fragmentation grenades near his home.

After receiving an anonymous phone call warning of a bomb in Figueres's private residence, police searched the area on Wednesday afternoon and found the grenades in an empty building about 100 yards (metres) away.

"This has been doubtless a little joke in bad taste and nothing more than that," Figueres told reporters during a news conference in his office before leaving for Nicaragua to attend a presidential inauguration there.
Figueres said he preferred to spend his time seeking a solution to Costa Rica's crippling internal debt mountain.
"I don't have time to spend on this kind of joke", he said, referring to the threat and the placing of the grenades.
Information Minister Alejandro Soto told Reuters that anti-explosives police were mobilised on Wednesday afternoon immediately after receiving a call warning of a bomb in Figueres' house.
Soto said police were investigating who might have planted the bomb, although he said Figueres had no enemies in Costa Rica, a generally peaceful nation which does not have an army.
